name: Acquired Dermis Elastic Tissue Disorder

criteria.description: Presence of asymptomatic, finely wrinkled, yellowish papules or plaques predominantly on sun-exposed skin
Histological evidence of marked loss or fragmentation of elastic fibers in the dermis on skin biopsy
Exclusion of inherited elastin disorders and other causes of dermal elastolysis
Lack of significant inflammatory infiltrate in affected skin areas

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: characteristic clinical presentation, histopathologic confirmation, and exclusion of other elastolytic disorders
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; no standardized criteria exist.

searchTerms: wrinkling of skin from sun exposure

pathognomonic.symptomName: Yellowish papular lesions on the skin

common.symptomName: Loss of skin elasticity in affected areas

searchTerms: skin changes mainly on sun-exposed areas
lesions on areas exposed to sun
mild thinning or wasting of skin
small visible blood vessels in skin

rare.symptomName: Secondary skin infections due to barrier disruption
searchTerms: skin infections due to barrier damage

genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; disorder is acquired
other: Skin biopsy showing marked fragmentation and loss of elastic fibers in the dermis using special stains (e.g., Verhoeff-Van Gieson)
Absence of significant inflammatory infiltrate on histology

distinguishingFeatures: Inherited disorder with generalized skin laxity
Presence of systemic involvement including pulmonary and cardiovascular abnormalities
Histology shows fragmented elastic fibers but with systemic manifestations
Yellowish papules with coalescing plaques mainly on neck and flexural areas
Calcification of elastic fibers on histology
Systemic involvement including ocular and cardiovascular complications
Histology shows basophilic degeneration of elastic fibers rather than loss
No papular lesions typical of acquired dermis elastic tissue disorder

redFlags: Development of systemic symptoms such as respiratory or cardiovascular compromise
Presence of ulceration or secondary infection in affected skin
